correctness.rationale: For a monotonic automaton, a word synchronizes a subset exactly when it synchronizes the subset's minimum and maximum, so exhaustive pair distances are sufficient. Every nondecreasing self-map of the normalized chain is generated, with counts C(2n-1,n). Exhausting all binary map pairs gives exact maxima 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9 for n=1,...,9. At n=9 exactly two unordered normalized map pairs have a pair at distance 9, yielding four ordered pairs. Independent forward BFS verifies the displayed hard pair and length-nine word.

value.rationale: The primary paper makes the fixed binary alphabet a substantive part of the asymptotic theory and leaves a large finite gap between its binary lower construction and general upper bound. The exact first departure from the elementary n-1 regime is therefore a natural boundary invariant. Identifying nine states as the first excess, together with a complete normalized extremal orbit, gives structural information about where genuinely quadratic-style delay begins rather than an arbitrary small census.
